clue.text: Generous, keeping one supplied in daily fare

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the food words enclose the numeral

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a British cleaning lady who comes in by the day
a good table means good food, the fare served
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone generous makes sure a single person is fed with the day's meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supplied in' is filler. A daily is British slang for a cleaning lady who comes by the day; a good table means good food.
explanation.definitionFit: A charitable person is open-handed and kind, freely giving to others.

clue.text: Strictly controlled kind of labour with expedition

parts.note: hard labour was a sentence of penal work, so hard is a kind of labour
with means together with, and
expedition in the sense of speed or haste, being fast

explanation.surface: A tightly run work gang sets off on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Rules that are inflexible and binding are said to be rigid, admitting no exceptions.

clue.text: Put out of Lincoln, say, to go to the country

definitions.meaning: Lincoln is an Oxford college; to send a student down from university for a while is the old term here
to retire to rural life, living like a countryman

explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the city or the president; it is Lincoln College, Oxford, from which an undergraduate may be temporarily suspended.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both temporary suspension from an Oxford or Cambridge college and moving to rural surroundings.

clue.text: Walked when young shaver showed the way

parts.note: Sweeney Todd, the demon barber of Fleet Street, is a famous shaver
to lead is to show the way; past tense led

explanation.surface: A small boy walked ahead, guiding others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'young shaver' suggests a little boy, but 'young' belongs to the definition and the shaver is the fictional murderous barber Sweeney Todd.
explanation.definitionFit: Toddlers walk with short unsteady steps, the gait of a small child learning to walk.

clue.text: Be a best man? A ring could be found in this cheap trading area

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters might be rearranged into another phrase

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a wedding ring could be bought in the discount section of a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in this' just links: rearrange the letters of BE A BEST MAN plus A RING.
explanation.definitionFit: A store's lowest floor is traditionally where cut-price goods are sold.

clue.text: Edges into Eastern church to get into shade

indicators.note: into means the first piece is put inside the following one

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
lips are the rims or edges of vessels

explanation.surface: Someone edges into an Orthodox church to escape the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get into' is link wording before the definition, which is the verb sense of shade: to overshadow.
explanation.definitionFit: To overshadow something, putting it in the shade, is to outshine or obscure it.

clue.text: Record of misdemeanours in class

definitions.meaning: British slang for a criminal record

explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for a criminal history and also a year group in a school.

clue.text: Veterans like this one only, oddly, fade away

indicators.note: oddly picks the first and third letters of the word only

parts.note: to die away is to fade gradually

explanation.surface: Old soldiers never die, they simply fade away.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the saying 'Old soldiers never die, they just fade away'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old person, a veteran in years, is affectionately called this.

clue.text: Artist not quite ready on time

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short by its final letter

parts.note: the ready, or readies, is British slang for cash

explanation.surface: A painter is almost prepared, but only just on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' looks like an adjective, but the readies is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet was the French Impressionist painter of water lilies.

clue.text: Follower of Richard less subtle about a Duke ()

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Follower of Richard less subtle about a Duke () (8)': empty brackets show text is missing, and CRUDER around A + D cannot give CRUSADER; the piece giving S is lost.
annotationWithheld.clue: Follower of Richard less subtle about a Duke ()

clue.text: Weighty field to study

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow or field
a den is a private study or room for work

explanation.surface: A heavy field of learning to master.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heavy as the metal lead is ponderous and weighty.

clue.text: Extremist, not Conservative, moving from the centre

indicators.note: not means the following letter is to be left out of the word before it

parts.note: a radical is a political extremist

explanation.surface: A political extremist, no Tory, drifts away from the middle ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests politics, the centre ground; the definition is about lines or motion outward from a centre point.
explanation.definitionFit: Spokes are radial: they spread outward from a hub.

clue.text: Father backing mother, perhaps, in evidence

indicators.note: backing means the following short word is turned round

parts.note: Pa is an informal name for a father
a mother is an example of a parent, as the perhaps signals

explanation.surface: A father supports the mother, as is plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obvious or visible is plainly seen, manifest.

clue.text: Banter he turns on one could be offensive

indicators.note: turns signals that the letters are twisted round into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's joking at another's expense could cause offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' rearranges BANTER HE to NEARTHEB; 'on' is a link and ONE follows unchanged. 'could be' leads to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A risqué joke that is close to indecent or hurtful is described with this idiom.

clue.text: Plan incompetent person doesn't' have

definitions.meaning: a plan or scheme in the mind
the idiom 'he hasn't a clue' or 'hasn't the faintest notion' describes a hopeless person

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a plan, and also the notion a clueless person is said not to have.

clue.text: Key subordinate to top man found to be a fool

parts.note: D is one of the musical keys
under means below in rank, subordinate to
the head is the person in charge

explanation.surface: The boss's trusted deputy turns out to be an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found to be a' is link wording.
explanation.definitionFit: A dim-witted person is a blockhead or dolt.

clue.text: She isn't wild about party for those on pleasure bent

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the party word
wild signals the letters of she isn't are thrown into disorder

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A woman is not keen on going to the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges SHE ISNT to HENISTS, which goes round the party word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure-seekers devote themselves to enjoyment, following the doctrine that pleasure is the highest good.

clue.text: Bridge player with singleton may be merciful

definitions.meaning: a bridge player holding a singleton in hearts holds just one card of that suit
the idiom pleading for compassion: have pity

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an appeal for compassion, and literally describes holding one card of a red suit.

clue.text: Fed up with such a meal?

definitions.text: Fed up with such a meal?

parts.words: Fed up with such a meal?
parts.note: read fed up as fed to the top or lofty, so the meal is an elevated tea; a teatime meal with cooked food

explanation.definitionFit: An early evening meal with a cooked dish, eaten in place of dinner in parts of Britain.

clue.text: Wine, in time, mostly become more palatable

indicators.note: in means the wine goes inside the shortened time word
mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a term is a fixed period of time
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: Wine, given time, mostly improves in flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts TERM to TER; 'become' is link wording before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Food with more flavour is more appetising, comparative of savoury pleasantness.

clue.text: Fruit 16 consumed

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Fruit 16 consumed (4)': ATE gives consumed, but nothing explains the D from '16' (16-across is DUNDERHEAD); likely an OCR misread of a word giving D, not verifiable.

clue.text: Restrict air passages of line in foreign location

indicators.note: in means the line letter is placed inside the foreign word

parts.note: strange in its sense of foreign or alien

explanation.surface: Someone abroad restricts the air ducts on one route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'location' is filler for where the L sits inside STRANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To throttle someone is to squeeze the throat and choke their breathing.

clue.text: One still hanging from tree as result of sin

definitions.meaning: a slow tree-dwelling mammal that hangs motionless from branches
one of the seven deadly sins, laziness

explanation.walkthrough: 'as result of' is link wording between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a slow-moving tropical tree mammal and the deadly sin of idleness.

clue.text: Life-preserving equipment fliers got on the way up

parts.note: the RAF is the Royal Air Force, the fliers

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Airmen got life-saving gear on the way up.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflatable floats carried on ships and aircraft keep survivors afloat.

clue.text: Trespasser in second target area

parts.note: the inner is the ring next to the bull on a target

explanation.surface: An intruder is found in the second zone of a shooting range.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Lord's Prayer, trespasses are sins, so a trespasser is a wrongdoer.

clue.text: Compensate for bad posture

parts.note: off means gone bad, as food goes off
set as the way one holds oneself, the set of the shoulders

explanation.surface: Someone works to correct their poor stance.
explanation.definitionFit: To counterbalance one thing against another is to make up for it.

clue.text: Discharge from English embassy

parts.note: a diplomatic mission is an embassy

explanation.surface: Someone is dismissed from the British embassy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given off, such as gas or light, is a discharge.

clue.text: Army entertainer

definitions.meaning: a great multitude, especially an army

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a large army and a person receiving guests.

clue.text: Oddly sedate about hazard marked for special attention

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the hazard word
oddly signals that the letters of sedate are arranged in a strange way

parts.note: a hazard is a risk

explanation.surface: A calm person, strangely, takes a chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like a call for alternate letters, but it rearranges the six letters of 'sedate' to ASTEED, wrapped round the hazard word.
explanation.definitionFit: Printed passages flagged with a star symbol are singled out for a footnote.
